INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.severity: must be read before anything else in this report
INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.cause: the first version of the scheduler-job test helper fired the pre-flight job body with the SUBPROCESS RUNNER replaced but not the STATE PATH. The job then did what it is built to do and wrote its own state. Replacing the process runner does not make a job body safe when the persistence happens in the parent.
INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.why_it_matters: the second file is not merely shorter - it asserts that TODAY's pre-flight passed, and today's pre-flight has not run (it fires 13:45 ET). A fabricated clearance for a day nothing has checked.
INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.caught_by: this suite's own 'no production file was written' test - the only reason it was noticed
INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.blast_radius: the running scheduler (pid 18096) loaded the real seven days at startup and reads the file only at startup, so it is unaffected; its own save at 13:45 ET rewrites the file correctly from memory. THE FILE SELF-HEALS IN ABOUT TWELVE HOURS. The exposure is a scheduler restart before then, which would load the fabricated clearance and let today's slots run without a pre-flight.
INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.what_i_did: fixed the helper so it cannot recur - every state path is redirected into tmp_path first, with the incident recorded in the test's own docstring
INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.what_i_could_not_do: attempted to restore the file; the action was BLOCKED, correctly - it is production runtime state and the standing constraint forbids editing it. I did not work around the block.
INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.restoration_is_reconstructed_not_guessed: the file's mtime was 11:47:28 on 08-25, the instant of that day's [PRE-FLIGHT] OK; _save_preflight_state keeps the last _PREFLIGHT_KEEP = 7 sorted days; every pre-flight that ran was OK (no FAILED line in any of those days' logs); and the last seven OK days ending 2026-08-25 are exactly the seven the scheduler reported restoring at 22:03:38.
INCIDENT_a_test_of_mine_overwrote_a_prod.restoration_command: python -c "import json,os; from pathlib import Path; p=Path('global_index/preflight_state.json'); d={k:True for k in ['2026-08-17','2026-08-18','2026-08-19','2026-08-20','2026-08-21','2026-08-24','2026-08-25']}; t=p.with_suffix('.tmp'); open(t,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(json.dumps(d,indent=2)); os.replace(t,p); print(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))"

where_it_blocks.the_judgement_call: the pre-flight exclusion is the one judgement call in the stage and it is written into the --verify-strict help text, the scheduler comment and the blocker's own evidence. A verification that could not run must not skip every slot of a trading day - the brief is explicit that UNKNOWN must not block shadow execution - and the 16:20 job runs after everything today has finished, so a non-zero exit there costs a visible failure and no trading.
